title: The Cancellation Fee Deducted From an Auto Loans Waiver Refund
content:
The cancellation fee deducted from the refund owed on waiver coverage financed with a loan of the Auto Loans line is read from the borrower's Personal Credit Cards account: the unredeemed reward points it carries, and the purchases posted to it in the last three months.

| Unredeemed reward points on the card | Card purchases posted in the last three months | Cancellation fee |
|---|---|---|
| At least 25000 | At least 12 | 0.00 |
| At least 5000, with either reading short of the row above | At least 3, with either reading short of the row above | 25.00 |
| Any other reading | Any other reading | The cancellation fee the product publishes |

The cancellation fee is 0.00 where the borrower's card carries at least 25000 unredeemed reward points and at least 12 card purchases have posted in the last three months.

It is 25.00 where that card carries at least 5000 unredeemed reward points and at least 3 card purchases have posted in the last three months, while either those points fall short of 25000 or those purchases fall short of 12.

It is the cancellation fee the product publishes for every other borrower.

## The fee at the edge of each row

A card carrying exactly 25000 points with 11 purchases in the last three months takes 25.00, the purchases falling short of 12 while both middle-row readings are met.

A card carrying 4999 points takes the fee the product publishes, whatever its purchase count.

A card carrying 40000 points with 12 purchases takes 0.00, so nothing is deducted from the unearned part.

## Where the two readings come from

The points reading is the unredeemed reward balance on the borrower's active card account in the Personal Credit Cards line. The purchase reading counts purchases posted to that card over the three months ending on the day of the cancellation, not their amounts.
